meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system governed by the Korean Commercial Act and specialized AML/CFT regulatory statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1992)

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1994)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the European Union and its Member States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Articles 19, 25, 543-620 on limited liability companies and trade names); Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (primary Korean AML/CFT statute requiring beneficial owner verification); Proceeds of Crime Act; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; FATF recommendations as implemented by the Financial Services Commission and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). For any Chinese parent or ultimate beneficial owner, the Chinese-side UBO certificate is obtained under the PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 on beneficial owner registration, effective November 1, 2024, with a Government-Only-Access disclosure standard.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registered Matters (Certificate of Incorporation of the Korean LLC, Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member: court-certified copy -> Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA Apostille Section). Consular Legalization route if the destination state is not an Apostille member: court-certified copy -> MOFA legalization/authentication -> Korean Embassy or Consulate in the destination jurisdiction -> destination Ministry of Foreign Affairs if required. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Clearance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (competent District Tax Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: NTS certificate -> Apostille by Korean MOFA Apostille Section. Consular Legalization route: NTS certificate -> MOFA consular legalization authentication -> Korean Embassy/Consulate in the destination state -> destination Ministry of Foreign Affairs where applicable. Apostille and consular legalization are never applied in the same chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation counsel, appointing the registered representative, and opening corporate bank accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / founding members of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized Board Resolution/Power of Attorney -> Hague Apostille by Korean MOFA if the destination state is an Apostille member. For non-Apostille destination states: notarized document -> MOFA consular legalization -> Korean Embassy/Consulate in the destination state. The route is determined solely by the destination state and the two methods are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Yuhan Hoesa (certified bilingual Korean/English copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members and Korean Notary Public, subsequently filed with the District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention destination: notarized copy of Articles -> Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-Apostille destination: notarized copy -> Korean MOFA legalization/authentication -> Korean Embassy/Consulate in the destination state -> destination Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate shareholder/investor from an existing relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's existing bank in the jurisdiction where the investor is incorporated and where the account is held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The Bank Reference Letter is signed by a bank officer and sealed by the bank; it is then notarized by a notary public in the bank's own jurisdiction. If that jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: notarized bank letter -> local Apostille. If that jurisdiction is not an Apostille member: notarized bank letter -> local Ministry of Foreign Affairs/consular route -> Korean Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction. The authentication path follows the country of origin of the bank document and is never linked to the Korean incorporation route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of UBO Identification / Beneficial Owner Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner register or competent corporate registry of each ultimate shareholder's jurisdiction; for Chinese ultimate shareholders, the PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 compliant UBO registration extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The UBO certificate is authenticated in the jurisdiction of the issuing authority. If that jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: issuing authority certificate -> local Apostille. If that jurisdiction is not an Apostille member: issuing authority certificate -> local competent authority -> consular legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction. The Korean incorporation support does not re-authenticate foreign documents under Korean law, and the two routes are never chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before KYC approval, every director, shareholder, UBO, authorized signer, corporate service provider contact, and relevant family member must be screened in real time against the KoFIU and Korean Financial Services Commission sanctions and terrorist designation lists issued under the Proceeds of Crime Act; the UN Security Council Consolidated List; OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; EU and UK consolidated sanctions; Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs designations; INTERPOL red notices; PEP databases such as World-Check and LexisNexis; and adverse media databases. Any PEP must receive senior management approval, documented source of wealth, source of funds, and enhanced transaction monitoring. A confirmed positive sanctions hit requires immediate freezing, refusal of business, and a Suspicious Transaction Report to KoFIU within 24 hours. All screening evidence must be archived for at least five years and refreshed no later than the day before any change in ownership or authorized signer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS / Internet Deungki-so) at www.iros.go.kr, together with the District Court Registry trade-name clearance desk and the National Tax Service Business Registration Number and Trade-Name Search system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean Commercial Act trade-name rules and registry practice for a Yuhan Hoesa, the registered corporate name must be written in Korean Hangul and cannot be registered solely in Roman letters. The English version may be used on contracts, invoices, and bank documents but must be a consistent transliteration of the Hangul name. The four-tier naming convention applied is: (1) distinctive Hangul identifier; (2) descriptive business purpose indicator; (3) the limited liability suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) a regional or brand qualifier if required by trademark clearance. Foreign words may be phonetically transliterated into Hangul in compliance with the National Institute of Korean Language transliteration rules, and the registered Hangul name becomes the statutory name for tax invoices, VAT, and payment rail onboarding.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of the registry officer's written rejection, the applicant's Korean counsel must file a written objection with the Chief Judge of the competent District Court Registry Division under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act, attaching the rejected application, the search report, the grounds for rejection, and any proposed corrected name. The Registry Division must rule within 30 days; if the objection is denied, an immediate appeal to the High Court must be filed within 14 days. In parallel, if the rejection is caused by a conflicting existing trade name, counsel may initiate judicial cancellation of the conflicting registration or, if trademark rights are implicated, administrative adjudication before the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board. A fresh name search with an alternative name is recommended in every rejection case to avoid unnecessary delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address is not acceptable for the Korean corporate registry, for NTS business registration, or for bank account opening. The District Court Registry requires a physical registered office with a specific building, floor, and unit written into the lease. The National Tax Service requires an actual domestic place of business before issuing the Business Registration Certificate and electronic tax invoice privileges. Korean banks will reject a virtual office for Direct Debit and Stripe Billing onboarding because the bank must verify the company's physical premises, lease, utility bill, nameplate, and responsible staff. For an ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud company, the minimum acceptable structure is a physical serviced office with dedicated desk, meeting room, company nameplate, mail handling, and VAT invoice address; a pure virtual office is not a lawful registered office and triggers NTS field audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 12-18% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the local tax office or registry officer during the first 18 months. The likelihood increases to 40-50% if a virtual address is used, VAT invoices are inconsistent, or the bank files a referral. Mandatory inspection checklist: (1) company nameplate and floor directory entry; (2) certified lease agreement in the company's name; (3) utility bill matching the registered address; (4) access control and CCTV logs; (5) employment contracts and attendance records; (6) active ERP/CRM hosting console, software licenses, or client projects; (7) bank statements and electronic tax invoice books; (8) corporate registers maintained and available at the registered office. A documented physical serviced office with active commercial substance materially reduces inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular service fee set by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; charged separately only for non-Apostille destinations and never in parallel with Apostille.
