incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-44 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), together with the Commercial Registration Act and Enforcement Decree as applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic submissions through the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a Yuhan Hoesa; the Articles of Association freely determine the capital amount. The subscribed capital must be paid or delivered in full before registration, evidenced by a bank-issued deposit certificate for cash contributions. There is no statutory blocked escrow account requirement beyond the restriction that incorporation capital deposited with the bank may not be withdrawn before completion of registration; non-cash contributions require a court-appointed appraiser's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF KR YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). RESOLUTION adopted on [Date], at [Place], pursuant to Articles 287-2 through 287-44 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, by the inaugural directors and executive officers of KR YUHANGHOESA (Limited Liability Company), a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, and recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of the governing body. WHEREAS the Company has been formed as a limited liability company with members whose liability is confined to their respective contributions, as set out in the Articles of Association; WHEREAS the members have duly subscribed to the contribution units shown in the contribution schedule and the aggregate stated capital of the Company is KRW [Amount]; WHEREAS the depository bank has issued a capital deposit certificate evidencing the receipt of the contributions to be paid at incorporation; WHEREAS the Articles of Association identify the intended registered office and the persons to serve as statutory officers; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows. FIRST, CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL: RESOLVED that the contribution schedule and subscription statements of all members be and are hereby ratified and confirmed; the total stated capital of the Company is fixed at KRW [Amount]; the Managing Director is directed to file the bank capital deposit certificate with the competent District Court at the time of incorporation registration and to take all steps necessary to protect the integrity of the Company's capital. SECOND, STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director and Executive Officer of the Company; [Name] be and is hereby appointed Auditor only if such appointment is required under the Commercial Act and the Articles; and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Each statutory officer shall hold office from the effective date of incorporation registration until lawful removal or replacement by the members. THIRD, BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Company maintain its principal banking relationship with [Bank Name], [Branch Name]; the Managing Director and any one other authorized officer jointly shall be designated signatories on all corporate accounts; the Managing Director is hereby authorized to execute account opening forms, banking service agreements, online banking enrollment, foreign currency transaction authorizations, and payment gateway instructions necessary for the vertical ERP-CRM cloud software business. FOURTH, REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company at [Address] be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory seat and principal place of business; the Managing Director is authorized to execute and deliver the lease or occupancy consent, to notify the District Court Registry, and to file the registered office details with the National Tax Service and any relevant administrative agency. FIFTH, GENERAL IMPLEMENTATION: RESOLVED that the statutory officers, acting jointly or singly as permitted, be and are hereby authorized to execute, sign, deliver and file all remaining documents, notices, tax registrations, foreign investment reports and other instruments required for incorporation, bank opening, employment, contracting, and the lawful commencement of cloud software services, and to engage outside counsel, notaries, valuers and tax advisors for such purposes. SIXTH: RESOLVED that certified copies of this Resolution be furnished to the Company's banks, accountants, the Commercial Registration Division, the National Tax Service, and any other authority reasonably requesting them. This Resolution is effective as of its adoption and shall be binding upon the Company and all members, directors, officers and successors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name screening, Articles of Association drafting, and foreign-capital screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO); Commercial Registration Division of the District Court of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through the Korean court registration portal to ensure that KR YUHANGHOESA is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered Korean company. If foreign members will hold ownership, assess whether a foreign investment report is required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and whether any non-resident documentation must be apostilled or consularized. Draft the Korean-language Articles of Association containing the mandatory clauses for a Yuhan Hoesa, including the corporate name, business object limited to information technology and vertical ERP-CRM cloud software services, total stated capital, contribution schedule of each member, registered office address, and the method of appointing executive officers. Obtain executed powers of attorney from all members and, for foreign entities, certified corporate registration extracts with sworn Korean translation.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search confirmation result
Draft Articles of Association in Korean
Passports or national identity cards of all members and proposed officers
Certificate of incorporation or corporate registry extract of any corporate member
Power of attorney from each member with apostille or consular legalization where applicable
Registered office lease agreement or landlord occupancy consent
English-to-Korean translation certificate for foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns a conflicting result, amend the company name and re-submit a revised name search at no additional court fee if the registration has not yet been filed. If the registry rejects the proposed registered office as incomplete, secure a corrected building consent or location certificate and resubmit the same application under the correction procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of incorporation capital and issuance of bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized to operate in the Republic of Korea, acting as depository institution for incorporation capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation account or designated contribution account in the name of KR YUHANGHOESA with a Korean commercial bank. Instruct each member to remit or deposit the full amount of their subscribed cash contribution in Korean won into the designated account. Verify the aggregated deposits against the contribution schedule in the Articles of Association and obtain a formal capital deposit certificate or receipt from the bank stating the Company's name, the total deposit amount, the date of deposit, and the restriction that the funds may not be withdrawn until incorporation registration is completed. If any member contributes non-cash assets, secure a court-appointed appraiser's valuation and execute a proper in-kind contribution transfer. The certificate will be presented to the District Court as conclusive evidence of capital payment.
required_dossiers: Member contribution schedule signed by all members
Inward remittance receipts or cash deposit slips for each contributing member
Bank-issued capital deposit certificate for the aggregate contribution amount
In-kind contribution appraisal report and transfer documents, if applicable
Directors' or executive officers' declaration confirming full payment or delivery of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or queries the source of funds, provide source-of-funds evidence such as bank statements, foreign remittance contracts, or gift/loan agreements, and request a corrected deposit certificate. If a member fails to contribute, amend the contribution schedule by supplemental members' resolution and re-sign the Articles before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and statutory officer consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public commissioned within the jurisdiction of the Seoul District Court or the competent District Court; Ministry of Justice notarial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the fully executed Articles of Association, powers of attorney, and officer consent letters to a Korean notary public for certification. The notary will verify the identity and legal capacity of each signatory, confirm that the Articles contain the mandatory clauses required for a Yuhan Hoesa under Articles 287-2 to 287-44 of the Commercial Act, and issue a notarial certificate attesting to the due execution of the document. If any member or officer is a foreign national, their passport copy and any power of attorney must be apostilled or consularized and accompanied by a notarized Korean translation before this step. The notarized Articles constitute the controlling constitutional document submitted to the registry and should be prepared in multiple counterparts for subsequent bank, tax, and civil defense filings.
required_dossiers: Original executed Articles of Association in Korean
Notarized powers of attorney from all members
Signed statutory officer consent and acceptance forms
Original apostilled corporate documents of foreign members with certified Korean translation
Passport copies of all individual shareholders and officers
Notary engagement instructions containing the registered office, capital amount, and officer designations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because of signature irregularity, re-execution defects, or missing translation, cure the deficiency by having the relevant members re-sign in the presence of the notary or by submitting a revised certified translation. If the notary requests additional corporate authority evidence from a foreign corporate member, obtain a fresh board resolution and certificate of incumbency and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory incorporation registration with the District Court commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; e-filing via the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company with the competent Commercial Registration Division. Attach the notarized Articles of Association, the bank-issued capital deposit certificate, statutory officer consent forms, evidence of the registered office, identification/residence documents of officers, and a power of attorney if a licensed agent is used. Pay the court registration fee and applicable registration license tax. The registrar will verify that all statutory requirements are satisfied, issue a Certificate of Registered Matters together with a company registration number separate from the tax identification number, and upload the registration record to the public company registry. Obtain several authenticated extracts and the certificate of the seal registration for use in opening bank accounts and executing commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Consent and appointment forms of statutory officers
Certified copies of identity documents for all officers
Registered office lease, ownership, or landowner consent evidence
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a written correction order, cure the identified defect within the stated compliance period, normally two weeks, by submitting a supplement or a revised notarized document. If the registrar rejects the application after correction, initiate an immediate appeal to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure. Corrected resubmissions filed within the compliance period are not normally subject to an additional registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and post-incorporation administrative startup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS); municipal or provincial administrative office where physical facilities are located, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after statutory incorporation registration, file a Business Registration Application with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office and obtain the Business Registration Certificate. Declare the business category as information technology consulting and software publishing services, including vertical ERP and CRM cloud software under ISIC 6201. Register for value-added tax and corporate income tax, open the corporate operating bank account, complete the corporate seal registration with the bank, and enroll the Company with the four major social insurance schemes, namely national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance. If foreign members hold ten percent or more of the Company, file the foreign investment report with KOTRA or an authorized foreign exchange bank to secure foreign direct investment protections.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters from the District Court
Notarized Articles of Association
Business Registration Application form
Identification card of the representative officer
Registered office lease or ownership evidence
Corporate bank account opening request forms
Four major social insurance registration forms
Foreign investment report receipt, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business location, submit a revised lease certificate or a written land owner consent and request expedited correction. If a foreign investment report was omitted, file a voluntary post-investment report through KOTRA before any capital outflow occurs and coordinate with tax counsel to mitigate any late-report penalty. If a tax registration is suspended, respond to the tax office notice within seven days and provide supplemental requested documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; ISIC 6201 is an information technology service rather than a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity. No industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing permit is triggered for a pure vertical ERP-CRM cloud software company.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; the Company requires only the standard Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service and the court-issued Certificate of Registered Matters to lawfully operate as a cloud software service provider.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment / Korea Environment Corporation, only if a future physical data center or large office fit-out is constructed; otherwise Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt; no full Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Registration, or pre-consultation tier is triggered by cloud-based software development and consulting operations because no physical facility threshold under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is crossed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the Company generates no wastewater, volatile organic compound, or hazardous waste streams from software operations. Standard municipal office waste segregation is required, and any incidental electronic waste from servers or office equipment must be disposed through licensed recycling vendors under the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable; as a pure digital/cloud ERP-CRM operator, the Company is not subject to Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or manufacturing workplace safety approval. Ordinary office occupancy must, however, comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Building Act fire safety requirements, and basic fire insurance obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr. Cross-border customs clearance: Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act at the competent district court registry and obtain the certificate of corporate incorporation and articles of incorporation. Step 2: Before commencing business, file the Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean head office, or electronically through the NTS HomeTax portal. Attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, office lease or address proof, passports of the directors and ultimate beneficial owner, the foreign investment notice filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if capital is inbound, and the bank-issued foreign investment remittance certificate. Step 3: Upon approval, the NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number. This number is the unified Tax Identification Number, Corporate Tax registration number, and VAT registration number; no separate VAT ID is issued. Step 4: Register the entity as an electronic tax invoice issuer on HomeTax, obtain the NTS corporate digital certificate, and integrate the accounting or ERP system with the NTS e-tax invoice API. Step 5: A non-resident corporate shareholder without a Korean permanent establishment is not required to obtain a Korean TIN solely because it owns the Korean Yuhan Hoesa. If the non-resident parent itself makes taxable supplies of electronic services into Korea, it must separately apply for the simplified foreign business VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act. Step 6: If treaty withholding relief is expected on dividends, the foreign parent should obtain a tax residence certificate from its own jurisdiction; this is submitted to the Korean payer or bank and is not a Korean TIN procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea has no U.S.-style check-the-box regime and no domestic-law pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. A Yuhan Hoesa whose head office or place of effective management is in Korea is a domestic corporation under the Corporation Tax Act and is taxed at entity level. Hybrid mismatch adjustments, where relevant, are applied under the international tax adjustment statutes, not by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold: every business operator in Korea must complete business registration before starting taxable business activities. A corporate Yuhan Hoesa is always a general VAT taxpayer. The simplified taxpayer status available to individual enterprises with annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000 is not available to a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing applies to all B2B taxable supplies. The VAT-registered supplier must issue a standard NTS e-tax invoice through the HomeTax e-invoicing system on or before the day following the supply date. The NTS provides an e-tax invoice API used by certified accounting and ERP systems for data transmission. Korea does not operate a real-time pre-clearance fiscal stamping regime; anti-fraud integrity is enforced through the mandatory HomeTax e-tax invoice pipeline, buyer and seller cross-matching, and the cash receipt system for end consumers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when exported from Korea under an accepted Korea Customs Service export declaration. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident and used or consumed outside Korea. For the vertical ERP or CRM cloud business, the Korean supplier must prove that the customer is a non-resident, the cloud service is contractually delivered for offshore use, the service is not consumed by the customer's Korean domestic establishment, the invoice states the service is for foreign consumption, and the foreign currency proceeds are received from abroad. Any cloud service consumed by a Korean branch or permanent establishment of the foreign customer is a domestic taxable supply at 10% VAT. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export supplies is creditable and can be refunded in the periodic VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS Export Declaration with acceptance number and export date for goods; not applicable to pure cloud services
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the foreign consignee and Korean exporter for goods
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order, and signed export contract
Bank-issued foreign exchange receipt certificate or inward remittance confirmation evidencing collection in foreign currency

For cloud or ERP SaaS: signed offshore service agreement, statement of work, service consumption logs, IP or geolocation records showing end-user access outside Korea, and a service acceptance certificate from the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export declarations, e-tax invoices, service agreements, and foreign exchange settlement records. If export zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply is recharacterized as domestic taxable, VAT is assessed at 10% on the full supply value, input VAT credits attributable to the supply are clawed back, penalty surcharges for false or unreported e-tax invoices are imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, and underpayment interest accrues. Deliberate false export claims can lead to criminal proceedings under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with fines and imprisonment, and the assessment may be reopened within the statutory limitation period for fraudulent or undisclosed matters.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (central bank) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bank of Korea administers the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, which divides all cross-border flows into current account and capital account items. Current account transactions, including trade receivables, software royalties, and service fees, are freely convertible; Korean resident companies may purchase KRW from or deposit KRW to their foreign exchange banks without prior approval, provided the transaction is supported by an invoice, contract, or customs declaration and a valid purpose code. The Korean won is also redeemable through foreign exchange banks for travel, education, and ordinary consumption within annual remittance quotas. Capital account flows, such as equity injections, intercompany loans, and M&A consideration, operate on a negative-list system: permitted transactions must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) through the designated foreign exchange bank, either before or after the transaction, based on the amount and nature. For profit remittance, shareholders must prove the actual receipt of paid-in capital, present audited accounts, show retained earnings calculation, and pay withholding tax; remittance is only allowed after such evidence is accepted. Surrender requirements still apply: all export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to Korea within six months of receipt and are subject to a conversion-to-KRW obligation, unless an approved offshore account is used. Overall, South Korea is generally current-account convertible but maintains a comprehensive notification and monitoring architecture for capital-account entries and exits, giving banks a central role in applying MOEF foreign-exchange regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and MOEF Implementing Rules, the statutory timeline for export proceeds is six (6) months from the date of receipt (or, in the case of usance L/C remittances, from the date of shipment). 100% of the foreign currency export receipts must be repatriated to an authorised foreign exchange bank in Korea and then sold for KRW or credited to a domestic foreign currency account within the same deadline, unless the exporter obtains an MOEF exemption (e.g., offshore retention account, intercompany netting, or reinvestment abroad). Failure to comply triggers administrative penalties and delays in future FX clearances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW + Foreign Currency)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, etc.) are not licensed as banks or electronic financial business operators under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; they cannot hold the entity’s principal deposit account or directly access Korea’s domestic clearance. Their use is legally limited to pre-funded payment facilitation through a licensed Korean bank. For this Korean LLC, the viability of relying on a fintech EMI as the primary treasury rail is Low; the EMI may only be used as a supplementary top-up channel after the Tier-1 domestic account is opened.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors are generally required to complete a one-time physical or notarised-proxy KYC session. Many Tier-1 Korean banks allow the responsible director to sign at a branch in person with passport and corporate seal, or to delegate through a power-of-attorney notarised at a Korean consulate and accompanied by an in-person meeting with the authorised representative. Remote video-only onboarding is rarely accepted for non-resident directors. Therefore, a physical presence or consular proxy opening is practically mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO disclosure for a Korean LLC with non-resident shareholders and possible nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registration, articles of incorporation, share register showing all shareholders and any holders with at least 25% UBO interest, notarised passport copies of all directors and UBOs, source-of-funds declaration for the initial equity capital, and a board resolution authorising the account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived shell risk triggered by a software/cloud business with no tangible local assets and reliance on Stripe Billing for revenue collection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid lease for the Korean office, utility and internet bills in the company name, labour contracts and social insurance records for at least one employee, VAT / business registration certificates, live website and product documentation, customer purchase agreements, and a clear explanation of the ERP/CRM service delivery model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border receipts originating from multiple overseas payment acquirers (Stripe, card networks) may raise concerns about KYC on ultimate counter-parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quarterly Stripe payout reports, customer master database excerpt, invoices with service descriptions and country breakdowns, sanctions/PEP screening results for all material contract counterparties, and an annual certified schedule of in-country business volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident shareholder through a third-party remitting bank or shareholder loan structure rather than a clean equity wire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed loan agreements or gift deed with notarisation, confirmed source-of-wealth documents (bank statements, sale contracts, inheritance certification), shareholder resolution classifying the remittance as paid-in capital, tax payment certificates, and the bank-issued FX transaction report pursuant to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must (a) open a foreign-currency account at a Tier-1 Korean FX bank; (b) submit a capital transaction declaration or FDI report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, using the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code for paid-in capital or foreign direct investment; (c) receive the SWIFT MT103 wire with accurate remittance notes; (d) have the bank issue a foreign currency deposit certificate; (e) convert the funds to KRW via the bank’s FX desk; (f) use the KRW deposit certificate for capital verification with the district court; and (g) complete any post-reporting to the MOEF or customs authority within the applicable deadline. All supporting documentation must be retained for at least five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the software/ERP/CRM vertical, outgoing settlement uses SWIFT MT103 for licence royalties, subcontracting fees, and dividends, supported by invoices, service agreements, and tax withholding receipts. Physical goods embedded in the software (e.g., edge servers) settle via commercial letters of credit or documentary collections, with shipping, insurance, and inspection documents. Dividend remittances require the board resolution, audited financial statements, and a bank-issued corporate tax settlement statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange forward contracts (up to 12 months, extendable with MOEF approval) for committed KRW/USD trade receivables and payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with a domestic bank, restricted to actual underlying foreign-currency contractual exposure
Cross-currency swaps for fixed-asset financing or long-term capital subscription based on a matching real cash-flow requirement, subject to the bank’s FX limit and MOEF reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Annual Financial Statement Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end anniversary plus 3 calendar months (e.g., 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year); a one-month extension may be applied for with prior NTS approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 20% additional tax on the underpaid corporate income tax plus 0.022% per-day interest; fraudulent or intentional omission: 40% additional tax; persistent non-payment can trigger asset seizure, withdrawal of tax clearance certificates, and judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements, Member Meeting Minutes, and Court Registration Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court of the Republic of Korea (Corporate Registration Division) through the Korean Supreme Court E-Registry system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Members' meeting must approve the financial statements within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; the approved statements and meeting minutes must be filed with the court within 1 week after such approval; anniversary-based deadlines apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 10,000,000 (approx. USD 7,500) under the Commercial Act for failure to file; repeated failure may lead to a court order for convening a meeting, enforcement of members' rights, and ultimately administrative strike-off or mandatory dissolution of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Update and Change Report (UBO / Substantial Shareholding Notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission (FSC); and the local District Court Registry for concurrent statutory register updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any transfer of membership interests that changes the ultimate beneficial owner; annual confirmation embedded in the financial statement filing cycle if no change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,500) for failure to report UBO changes; overdue register amendments can invalidate board or member resolutions and expose directors to civil liability; persistent failure may be treated as a ground for corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Business Performance Report (conditional - applies only if non-resident ownership is 5% or more or the company is registered as a foreign-invested enterprise)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the preceding fiscal year-end (or by the fiscal-year anniversary rule if a different accounting period is approved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 3,000,000 (approx. USD 2,250) per violation; non-filing may lead to loss of foreign investment protection and privileges, and, with repeated omission, cancellation of the foreign-invested enterprise status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is legally required to appoint a certified public accountant (CPA) for external audit if any of the following thresholds is breached at the most recent fiscal year-end: (i) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); (ii) the company is a listed issuer or is a financial company under the External Audit Act; (iii) the company's annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion (approx. USD 75 million) together with a headcount of 500 or more employees, per the SME criteria under the Presidential Decree; (iv) the company has 500 or more employees regardless of asset size; or (v) it is designated by the regulator as a public-interest entity. For such entities, the audit must be performed by a licensed CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) under the Korean External Audit Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), fully aligned with IFRS as issued by the IASB, is mandatory for all publicly accountable entities and threshold-exceeding companies. Non-publicly accountable LLCs may elect Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for small and medium enterprises (SME-K GAAP) if they stay below the mandatory audit threshold. The chosen framework must be applied consistently and audited under Korean audit standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Financial Transaction Reports Act and the Commercial Act, the LLC must maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds 25% or more of the membership interests or control rights. Any transfer of membership interests or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the company registry and, when applicable, to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 calendar days from the change date. There is no standalone annual UBO return; nonetheless, the LLC must perform an annual confirmation of UBO data at the end of each fiscal year, embedded in the statutory financial statement filing and corporate electronic registry renewal, and the updated register must be available for inspection by the court and financial authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,200 per annum for a professional registered agent and virtual office arrangement in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 20,000 per audit engagement for a software and CRM cloud company if the mandatory audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% CIT headline marginal rate applicable to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 2.4% Local Income Tax surcharge (10% of the corporate income tax), producing a combined top effective rate of 26.4%. The progressive rate schedule under Article 55 of the Korean Corporate Income Tax Law (CITL) is: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% above KRW 300 billion, in each case exclusive of the 10% local surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Yuhan Hoesa, being a vertical ERP/CRM cloud software entity (ISIC 6201), is eligible for (i) the R&D tax credit under Article 10 of the CITL and Article 10-2 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA), allowing an additional deduction of up to 30% of qualifying cloud-software research and development expenditure against corporate income tax for new growth engine technologies; (ii) tax credits for facilities investment in cloud data centers; (iii) preferential rates available under the Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone regimes, including full corporate income tax exemption for 5 years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech businesses; (iv) special tax support for SMEs, including reduced CIT rates of 5-9% on the first KRW 200 million for qualifying small and medium enterprises; and (v) the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA) foreign tax credit mechanism to eliminate double taxation on cross-border cloud licensing income. Any tax holiday or credit is subject to Korean economic substance review, and the effective rate after incentives could be reduced to near 0% for a newly established qualifying free-zone entity, although the statutory headline rate remains 24% + 2.4% local surcharge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Foreign Corporations (法人稅申告書) filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing system at www.hometax.go.kr, using the statutory form for a non-resident corporation with a Korean domestic place of business (CITL Article 60 and Article 91; the return is commonly designated as the 'Foreign Corporation Corporate Income Tax Return' attached to the annual CIT return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a mandatorily required separate semi-annual tentative return for corporations whose prior-year taxable income exceeded KRW 500 million or whose business year exceeds 6 months (CITL Article 63).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 of the following year for a December 31 fiscal year-end. The mid-year tentative return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the first 6 months of the fiscal year, i.e., by September 30 for a calendar-year taxpayer, together with payment of one-half of the tentative tax due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Identification of the Taxpayer and Korean Domestic Place of Business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name of the Yuhan Hoesa, Business Registration Number, global entity identifier, registered address of the domestic place of business in Korea, representative director details, industry code (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210), and date of incorporation or foreign corporation registration with the Korean tax authorities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must designate and register a 'domestic place of business' in Korea under CITL Article 94; if no actual fixed place exists, a deemed domestic place of business is established by operation of law. The filing system will reject the return if the foreign entity identifier and the Korean domestic business operator registration are inconsistent. Cross-border entities should ensure that the Korean branch registration, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act filing, and the NTS corporate registration all reference the same ultimate beneficial owner to avoid mismatched data referral for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Total Gross Revenue and Ordinary Income (Period Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total gross revenue derived from the Korean source business, including ERP cloud software subscription fees, CRM SaaS recurring fees, implementation services, maintenance, support, customization revenue, and any license or royalty-type income from software. Foreign-source income attributable to the Korean domestic place of business must also be included where the Yuhan Hoesa is taxed on its worldwide income as a domestic corporation, or only Korean-source income for a non-resident foreign corporation branch.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxpayer must perform a Korean-source income analysis under CITL Article 93. In particular, income from the provision of cloud-hosted ERP/CRM services to Korean customers should be analyzed under the 'services' or 'business profits' classification rather than as royalty income if the customer does not obtain a copy of the software for independent exploitation. Permanent establishment exposure arises if the foreign enterprise has a dependent agent or a fixed place in Korea through which the cloud service is concluded. For subscription contracts billed through Stripe Billing or direct debit, the revenue recognition date, the invoicing currency conversion, and the source-of-income attribution must all be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Deductible Expenses, Cost of Sales, and Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report cost of goods sold, salaries, rent, cloud hosting costs, intercompany fees, depreciation, R&D expenses, marketing, and general administrative expenses. Where the accounting net income has been adjusted for corporate income tax purposes, enter the reconciliation items such as non-deductible entertainment expenses, non-deductible reserves, depreciation differences, and unrealized intercompany profit eliminations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation taxed on its Korean domestic place of business, only expenses that are actually incurred for the domestic business and properly evidenced by adequate accounting records are deductible (CITL Article 91(3)). The deduction of head-office general administrative expenses allocated to the Korean PE must satisfy the arm-length cost-allocation standards under Article 6 of the ITAA. International payment for cloud infrastructure, software royalties, and management fees must be supported by written agreements, and any excessive allocation to a foreign head office may be denied, triggering TP adjustment and a 40% additional tax penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Taxable Income Determination (Taxable Income Before Carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income, which is the adjusted net income after application of tax adjustments, including non-taxable income, non-deductible expenses, special deductions for R&D, loss carryforward deduction, and the 'deemed income' recomputation arriving at the final taxable income subject to the progressive rates of Article 55.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Yuhan Hoesa, if losses are carried forward, a strict continuity test requires that the same business be continuously operated and that the controlling shareholders have not substantially changed; otherwise, the carryforward deduction is denied for up to the difference between the acquired entity and the pre-existing loss base. Loss carryforward of 5 years as set out in this whitepaper is the applicable conservative statutory tracking period used for the ERP/CRM vertical, although tax reform history provides longer relief for SMEs. Non-resident corporations must also complete the separate 'Foreign Corporation Income Attribution Statement' showing the allocation of net income attributable to the Korean PE, with documentary evidence of intercompany recharge and cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Corporate Income Tax Computation and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory CITL Article 55 progressive rates to the taxable income computed in Box 4, then subtract (i) the R&D tax credit, (ii) the foreign tax credit, (iii) the tax credit for investment in cloud/R&D facilities, (iv) the SME tax credit, and (v) any prior-year prepayments, to arrive at the current-year corporate income tax liability. Add the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge (resident surcharge) to determine the total combined corporate tax for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are entitled to the same tax credits as domestic corporations only for income attributable to the Korean domestic place of business. Foreign tax credits must be substantiated with foreign tax return copies and official tax payment receipts. If the foreign cloud-platform provider's income is characterized as royalty income rather than business income, the final CIT computation may be replaced with final withholding at 22% (20% CIT plus 2% local surcharge) with no right to claim deductions, so the taxpayer must confirm the characterization filing stance before submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Tax, Prepayments, and Final Net Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the total tax payable after offsetting the mid-year tentative payments, wage withholding tax credits, and any tax-withheld-at-source credits on Korean-sourced interest, dividends, and royalties. The net amount payable, plus any penalty and interest for late payment, is then scheduled for payment through HomeTax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the Yuhan Hoesa has received Korean-source interest, dividend, or royalty income from which 22% was withheld at source, attach the withholding tax certificates issued by the withholding agent. The foreign tax credit available against the Korean CIT must not exceed the limitation calculated on the same Korean-source income. Any profit repatriation through dividend resolution by the shareholders will be subject to a separate shareholder-level withholding tax (22%, including local surcharge) unless a double tax treaty reduces the rate; the company acts as withholding agent and must remit the tax by the 10th day of the month following the distribution to the NTS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Representations, Signatures, and Attached Documents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal representative's signature, tax accountant certification, audited financial statements, schedule of tax adjustments, foreign corporation information statement, intercompany transaction statement, local file / master file disclosure, and beneficial owner statement for treaty-reduced withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an overseas parent or ultimate owner of the Yuhan Hoesa, attach a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), power of attorney, and documentary proof of beneficial ownership when claiming treaty relief. Failure to attach the required TP disclosure schedules can itself trigger a KRW 30 million civil penalty under ITAA Article 11, even if the underlying tax is correct.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual corporate income tax return attracts a non-payment penalty of 0.022% per day up to a maximum of approximately 9% of the unpaid tax, plus a separate 20% error penalty for under-reported amounts and a 40% penalty for failure to pay, with the exact calculation governed by Articles 47-2 through 47-5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Failure to file altogether produces an un-reported tax addition of 20% of the tax unpaid; filing a fraudulent or false return increases the penalty to 40%, and if the unpaid tax exceeds a statutory threshold, criminal prosecution under CITL Article 109 may result in imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Mid-Year Tentative Corporate Income Tax Return for Foreign Corporations (Article 63 CITL), filed in HomeTax for the first 6 months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual; applicable only where the prior year taxable income exceeded KRW 500 million, or where the business year exceeds 6 months, or where the corporation is newly established and does not satisfy the statutory exemption threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the first 6 months of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, the deadline is September 30. The tentative tax equals one-half of the amount computed by applying the previous year's tax rates to the first half-year taxable income, reduced by any income already subject to final withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the net income for the first six months, adjusted for the same tax adjustments used in the annual return, and compute the tentative taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations whose Korean PE has losses in the first half but expects annual profitability must still file a zero-payment tentative return; failure to file triggers a penalty of 0.5% of the tentative tax. For the vertical ERP/CRM cloud entity, the half-year cutoff should match the internal management accounts, and any revenue deferred under Korean tax law should be excluded from the tentative base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Prior Year Tax Base Recomputation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If the corporation has no first-half net income, it may elect to recompute the tentative base by applying the prior year's annual taxable income for the corresponding half-period on a reasonable basis, as expressly permitted by statute.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The election is irrevocable for that fiscal year and must be reflected consistently in the annual return; the Yuhan Hoesa's tax preparer should analyze the elasticity of the ERP/CRM subscription revenue recognition before electing, because customers using automatic renewal via Stripe Billing may generate recognized revenue early in the second half. This election cannot be used to reduce the tentative liability below the minimum amount determined by the NTS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tentative Tax and Payment Voucher
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the tentative corporate income tax at the preceding year's effective rate plus the 10% local surcharge, then offset the preliminary withholding credits, and remit the net amount via HomeTax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment voucher must identify the mid-year period as 'mid-year' and the withholding tax certificate number; a foreign currency remittance through an overseas parent accountant must be reported on the Foreign Exchange Transaction Report attached to the tentative return, otherwise a separate Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalty may be imposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the tentative return or underpayment of the tentative tax triggers a daily overdue interest rate of 0.022% until paid, a 20% underreporting penalty on the deficit, and additional criminal exposure if the underpayment is intentional and in excess of KRW 300 million. The NTS will immediately assess and collect the provisional deficiency before the annual return is filed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on outbound dividends (20% corporate income tax withholding as final tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge), as provided under CITL Article 98(5) and the Local Tax Act. The 22% rate applies to dividend distributions made by the Yuhan Hoesa to its foreign corporate shareholders unless a bilateral double tax treaty (DTA) reduces the rate; typical Korean DTA rates for portfolio dividends range from 10% to 15%, and for substantial shareholdings up to 5% to 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must deliver to the Yuhan Hoesa as withholding agent a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a Beneficial Owner Declaration (Form required by NTS), and a written treaty-relief application form (Application for Income Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty) before the dividend payment is made. The foreign shareholder must be the beneficial owner, cannot be an intermediary, and must prove that it has substantial business activity outside Korea; the Yuhan Hoesa must submit the application together with the withheld tax return by the 10th day of the following month. If the treaty application is approved, the withholding agent refunds any excess withholding within 30 days; if the TRC is incomplete, the NTS will assess the full 22% withholding and add a 30% additional tax based on the under-withholding. For the ERP/CRM vertical, the treaty analysis must additionally distinguish a dividend paid out of accumulated Korean-source profits from a distribution of technical-services income already taxed on a gross basis, because a treaty article applicable to services may recharacterize the distribution as a servicing fee if the underlying reserve is fictitious.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties paid by the Yuhan Hoesa to non-residents are subject to the same statutory 22% final withholding (20% CIT plus 2% local surcharge) under CITL Article 98(3) and Article 98(4). Under most Korean DTAs, the treaty-reduced rate for interest is 10-15%, and for royalties is 10-15%; however, for software subscription income in an ERP/CRM cloud model, a critical distinction applies: if a Korean customer receives only a hosted cloud service without a transfer of the software copyright, the income is classified as business profits (Article 7 of the DTA) and is not subject to Korean WHT unless the foreign recipient has a Korean PE, whereas if the same payment is recharacterized as royalties for the right to use computer software, the 22% statutory WHT applies unless the DTA rate under the royalty article is lower. The Yuhan Hoesa should draft customer contracts to state that the payment is for cloud subscription services, not for the license of software, to avoid the use of royalty withholding and to mitigate economic double taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 500 million (KRW 5억, approximately USD 400,000) in annual cross-border related-party transactions aggregated across all contract types; if this threshold is exceeded, the Yuhan Hoesa must prepare the Local File under Article 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA). In addition, the Master File must be prepared where the multinational group has consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more, and a Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) is mandatory for a group with consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more. Routine intercompany transactions below the threshold remain subject to the arm-length principle but do not require the statutory documentation file unless specifically demanded by the NTS.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) statute; instead, economic substance is enforced through the 'actual control test' under Article 8 of the ITAA (the so-called abuse-of-rights doctrine), under which a corporate vehicle lacking genuine business purpose, sufficient employees, operating premises, and actual decision-making functions in Korea can be disregarded or recharacterized. For a KH Yuhan Hoesa operating a vertical ERP/CRM cloud business, the NTS applies the substance-over-form rule to determine whether the Korean entity is the true recipient of the cloud service revenue or merely a service-based pass-through shell. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) analysis requires that the strategic product development, software development, and cloud infrastructure deployment be performed by personnel based in Korea, that the board of directors for the Korean entity convene in Korea, and that the financial accounts reflect the actual commercial activity in Korea; a pure invoice-raising entity with a foreign decision center would be treated as a sham for CITL purposes and as a controlled foreign company of its foreign parent where the passive income is concerned. The NTS also applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Articles 4-6 of the ITAA to reallocate income to the jurisdiction where the economically significant functions, assets, and risks are located, with particular scrutiny on the attribution of software-licensing intangibles between the Korean entity and the foreign group IP holder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cloud subscription and ERP/CRM implementation revenue from the Korean corporate income tax return, fabrication of fictitious expenses, use of false invoices to inflate tax deductions, or concealment of the existence of the Korean domestic place of business from the NTS. In the Yuhan Hoesa context, this includes routing Korean customer payments through an overseas Stripe account without reporting the income as Korean-source, or causing the Korean LLC to be treated constructively as a non-resident while the actual management and cloud services occur in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3, the NTS will impose an additional tax of 40% of the tax evaded for fraudulent filing; under Article 47-4, a 20% penalty applies for un-reported tax; under CITL Article 109, a representative who deliberately evades corporate income tax is subject to imprisonment for not more than 5 years or a fine of not less than the amount evaded and not more than 5 times the amount evaded; the evasion penalty does not preclude the tax authority from collecting the principal tax plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS will pierce the corporate veil where fraud or gross negligence is proved: directors who participated in the concealment of revenue are jointly and severally liable with the corporation for the unpaid corporate income tax, penalties, and interest under Korean commercial law principles and tax law doctrine developed under Article 42 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. In addition, the NTS may blacklist the director and issue a travel ban preventing departure from Korea until the outstanding tax is secured; where the evasion exceeds statutory thresholds, the director faces criminal imprisonment for up to 5 years, and the court may additionally order forfeiture of benefits and a fine of 5 times the evaded tax. Civil liability extends to the restoration of corporate property misappropriated through the shell arrangement, and the director is banned from serving as a director of any newly incorporated Korean company for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse, Shell Entity, and Failure to Meet Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming reduced Korean dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax rates under a Korean double tax treaty on outbound payments to a foreign parent that has no substantive business activity, no employees, no real office, and is resident solely for tax purposes in a low-tax jurisdiction; similarly, using a Korean shell company (the Yuhan Hoesa) as a conduit to license software from an offshore entity that has no real management or development substance, thereby artificially reducing Korean-source income. The triggering conduct includes submitting a Tax Residence Certificate without beneficial-ownership evidence, or structuring a chain of payments through a conduit country solely for the purpose of obtaining a lower DTA rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, the NTS may deny the benefit of the tax treaty where the main purpose of the arrangement is to obtain treaty benefits; the withholding rate will be restored to the full statutory 22% (20% CIT plus 2% local surcharge), and additionally a 30% penalty tax on under-withholding can be imposed under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Where the Korean entity is a fake shell, the NTS may tax the beneficial owner as the deemed Korean domestic enterprise, thereby converting the gross-basis withholding tax into net-basis corporate income tax at the 24% headline rate plus the 2.4% local surcharge, creating a substantially larger tax demand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts have applied the substance-over-form principle to disregard the separate legal personality of a conduit corporation when it is used as a vehicle for tax evasion; in such cases, the foreign parent and the Korean directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid taxes. Directors face personal assessment for the tax amount under the comprehensive liability clause, asset seizure orders, provisional attachment of personal bank accounts, travel restrictions, and criminal indictment for aiding and abetting tax evasion, with a maximum term of 5 years in prison. Additionally, the Financial Supervisory Service may impose a concurrent administrative fine for failing to report the beneficial owner under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, and the Korean customs and foreign exchange authorities may revoke the corporate foreign exchange business registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Misuse of Intercompany Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or submit the Local File and Master File when the Yuhan Hoesa transacts in excess of KRW 500 million annually with its foreign parent, sale of ERP/CRM software or cloud services to a connected non-resident at prices below the arm-length rate, payment of excessive royalties or management fees to the foreign parent without any actual service, or allocation of a disproportionate share of group profit to a low-tax jurisdiction by claiming that the key software intangibles are owned abroad, while the actual development is carried out in Korea. Another fatal infringement is the failure to report the intercompany transaction schedule on the annual corporate income tax return, or mischaracterizing a cross-border loan from the parent as equity to avoid interest withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 11(1) of the ITAA, failure to submit the Local File or Master File gives rise to a civil penalty of up to KRW 30 million, and the NTS may concurrently adjust the entity's taxable income under Article 4, 5, and 6 of the ITAA by applying the arm-length principle; the tax adjustment carries an additional tax equal to 40% of the under-reported tax amount for improper transfer pricing declarations under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and if the adjustment exceeds KRW 500 million, the case is automatically transferred to the National Tax Investigation Bureau for criminal review. Filing false TP documentation also triggers the criminal provisions of Article 109 (falsification) and Article 110 (fraud) under the CITL, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 5 times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign the false transfer pricing documentation are personally liable for the additional tax assessment to the extent that the corporate assets are insufficient, on the theory that the director has breached the duty of care owed to the company and its creditors. The NTS may impose a departure ban, place the director on the black-list for large delinquent taxpayers, and apply a separate penalty of percent from 10% to 40% on the director's personal remuneration. In a criminal proceeding, the director, as the person who actually executes the false declaration, is the primary defendant and may receive a sentence of up to 5 years in prison; in egregious cases involving the creation of sham contracts and false invoices, the indictment will include charges of document forgery and fraud under the Korean Criminal Act, under which cumulative sentences can exceed 10 years. Additionally, the director must make full civil restitution of the unpaid tax plus interest, and is prohibited from leaving Korea until the tax lien is satisfied or a payment guarantee is posted.
